title: The Hero
description: The first thing visitors see. Makes or breaks the first impression.
tips: Keep copy concise: aim for 6–8 words in the headline
Use one clear call-to-action, not five
Hero images should support, not distract from, the message

title: Navigation
description: The roadmap to your content. Should be invisible until needed.
tips: Maximum 7 items in primary navigation
Logo always links home
Current page should be visually distinct

title: The Fold
description: The visible area before scrolling. People do scroll, but this space still gets disproportionately more attention.
tips: Core value proposition must be above the fold
Include a scroll indicator if content continues
Don't cram everything in. Tease what's below

title: Typography Hierarchy
description: Visual hierarchy through type creates scannable content.
tips: Limit to 2–3 font families maximum
Use consistent heading sizes (H1 > H2 > H3)
Body text: 16–18px for screens

title: Whitespace
description: The breathing room that makes content digestible.
tips: More whitespace often reads as more premium
Use consistent spacing units (8px base)
Let important elements breathe

title: Footer
description: The last impression. Where skeptical visitors look for legitimacy.
tips: Include contact info and social links
Secondary navigation for SEO
Copyright and legal links belong here

title: Content Sections
description: The middle of the page. Where features, proof, and objections actually get addressed.
tips: Group related content into clear, scannable sections
Alternate layout patterns (image-left, image-right) to avoid monotony
Every section should answer one question the visitor still has

title: Color & Contrast
description: Color sets the mood, but contrast is what actually makes text legible and buttons findable.
tips: Body text needs at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background
Never use color alone to convey meaning; colorblind users need a second cue
Limit an interface to 2–3 main colors plus neutrals

title: Calls-to-Action
description: The single most important click on the page. Everything else exists to lead someone here.
tips: One primary CTA per section; competing buttons dilute both
Use action verbs: "Start Your Trial" beats "Submit"
Make it visually distinct from every other button on the page

title: Responsive Design
description: More than half of web traffic is mobile. Design for the smallest screen first, then expand.
tips: Design mobile-first, then scale up to tablet and desktop
Touch targets need to be at least 44×44px
Test at real breakpoints, not just by shrinking your browser window
